ACT head atlas: what each of the 48 attention heads does

Two public ACT checkpoints from LeRobot, one per ALOHA simulation task. Each has 48 attention heads that run at inference: 4 encoder self-attention layers of 8 heads (enc0 to enc3, mixing camera, joint and latent tokens), the decoder's cross-attention (cross, where each action step reads the scene) and the decoder's self-attention (dself, whose output is constant, so scaling it acts as a fixed internal offset). A head is edited by scaling its 64 columns of the block's out_proj weight: x0 removes it, x2 doubles it.

How to read the columns.

  • Open-loop effect: RMS change of the 100-step action chunk (normalized action units, all 14 joints) when the head is scaled, averaged over the recorded step-0 frames of the 41 x 41 start grid. No rollout: recorded states are fed to the edited policy. For insertion the peg and socket grids are averaged.
  • Signal lost: 1 minus the variance of the edited step-0 chunk over the grid poses, divided by the original's. Positive means the head carries object-position signal that is lost without it (cube for transfer cube, mean of peg and socket for insertion).
  • Failure-map overlap: Spearman correlation over the grid of a head's step-0 effect map with the smoothed failure map of the original policy. It was the pre-registered way to pick 5 heads for a recheck.
  • Closed-loop gain: change of the primary score, in points, over 500 design seeds (20000 to 20499) when that single head is scaled, with seeds fixed/broken and the exact McNemar p. This is a screen of 96 arms; the p values are not corrected and several large ones will be noise. Split half: the 15 arms rechecked on seeds 20500 to 20999 and whether the sign held.

Everything here comes from design seeds and recorded grid states, which the agent used to choose its edits. None of it is test evidence. The held-out results are in the referee's verdicts, experiments/<task>/test/VERDICT.md. The atlas numbers also did not explain the edits. On transfer cube the head the written hypothesis relied on (enc3.h4) loses almost no cube signal when removed (-0.001), and on both tasks the pre-set tracking numbers did not move as predicted (see each task's report/report.md). Built by python publish/build_atlas.py from committed files only.
